questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Asymptotes of a Horizontal Hyperbola Given in Standard Form
questions.worked_solution:
The standard equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

For a horizontal hyperbola, the equations of the asymptotes are

$$
y-k=\pm \frac{b}{a}(x-h).
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
(h,k)=(5,0),\,a=\sqrt{9}=3,\,b=\sqrt{16}=4.
$$

 

Therefore, the asymptotes are given by

$$
\begin{aligned}y-0 & =\pm (\frac{4}{3})(x-5) \\ y & =\pm \,\frac{4}{3}(x-5).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Calculate the asymptotes of the hyperbola $16{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}-64x-2y+47=0.$
questions.worked_solution:
To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in standard form, we need to group the $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}16{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}-64x-2y+47 & =0 \\ (16{x}^{2}-64x)+(-{y}^{2}-2y)+47 & =0 \\ 16[{x}^{2}-4x]-[{y}^{2}+2y]+47 & =0 \\ 16[(x-2)^{2}-4]-[(y+1)^{2}-1]+47 & =0 \\ 16(x-2)^{2}-64-(y+1)^{2}+1+47 & =0 \\ 16(x-2)^{2}-(y+1)^{2} & =64-1-47 \\ 16(x-2)^{2}-(y+1)^{2} & =16 \\ \frac{16(x-2)^{2}}{16}-\frac{(y+1)^{2}}{16} & =\frac{16}{16} \\ \frac{(x-2)^{2}}{1}-\frac{(y+1)^{2}}{16} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

The asymptotes of a horizontal hyperbola

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1
$$

are given by 

$$
y-k=\pm \frac{b}{a}(x-h).
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
h=2,\,k=-1,\,a=\sqrt{1}=1,\,b=\sqrt{16}=4.
$$

Therefore, the asymptotes of the hyperbola are

$$
\begin{aligned}y+1 & =\pm \frac{4}{1}(x-2) \\  & =\pm 4(x-2).\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Asymptotes of a Vertical Hyperbola by Completing the Square
canonical_examples.problem: Calculate the asymptotes of the hyperbola $y^2 - x^2 - 2y = 0.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in standard form, we need to group the $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}-2y & =0 \\ ({y}^{2}-2y)-{x}^{2} & =0 \\ (y-1)^{2}-1-{x}^{2} & =0 \\ (y-1)^{2}-{x}^{2} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

The asymptotes of the vertical hyperbola

$$
\dfrac{(y-k)^2}{a^2} - \dfrac{(x-h)^2}{b^2} = 1
$$

are given by 

$$
y-k=\pm \dfrac{a}{b}(x-h) .
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
(h,k) = (0,1), \qquad a = \sqrt{1} = 1, \qquad b= \sqrt{1} = 1.
$$

Therefore, the asymptotes of the hyperbola are

$$
\begin{aligned}y-1 & =\pm x.\end{aligned}
$$
